tasks.title: Distances by breadth-first search
tasks.statement: Write a function bfs_distances(graph, start): graph is a dictionary "vertex → list of neighbors" (vertex names are strings). Return a dictionary "vertex → minimum number of edges from start" for all reachable vertices.
tasks.hint: A queue and a distance dictionary (which doubles as the "visited" set): a neighbor gets dist[v] + 1 if it has not been visited yet.

tasks.title: Connected components
tasks.statement: Write a function count_components(graph): the number of connected components of an undirected graph (a dictionary "vertex → list of neighbors", each edge recorded in both directions). The check feeds a chain of 200,000 vertices, so the traversal must be iterative (recursion will crash).
tasks.hint: For each unvisited vertex start a traversal with a stack or queue and increment the component counter.

tasks.title: Cycle in an undirected graph
tasks.statement: Write a function has_cycle(graph): True if an undirected graph (each edge recorded in both directions, no loops or multiple edges) contains a cycle. During the traversal remember the vertex's "parent": going back to it does not count as a cycle.
tasks.hint: DFS/BFS with (vertex, parent): if a neighbor has already been visited and is not the parent, a cycle is found.

tasks.title: Topological sort
tasks.statement: Write a function topo_order(graph): graph is a directed graph without cycles, "vertex → list of the vertices it points to". Return an order of vertices in which each one comes before all of its descendants; of the several valid orders, take the lexicographically smallest (in Kahn's algorithm choose the smallest ready vertex, using a heap). If there is a cycle, return an empty list.
tasks.hint: The indegree of each vertex; the heap holds the vertices with zero; pop one and decrease the indegree of its neighbors. If not all vertices were output, there is a cycle.

tasks.title: Bipartite graph
tasks.statement: Write a function is_bipartite(graph): True if the vertices of an undirected graph can be colored with two colors so that the ends of every edge have different colors. The graph may be disconnected.
tasks.hint: A traversal with coloring: a neighbor gets the opposite color; if an already colored neighbor has the same color, the graph is not bipartite.

tasks.title: Number of islands
tasks.statement: Write a function count_islands(grid): grid is a list of strings made of '1' (land) and '0' (water). An island is a group of land cells connected horizontally and vertically. Return the number of islands. The check feeds a 1000×1000 field, so no recursion.
tasks.hint: For each '1' cell not seen yet, run a traversal (stack) in four directions and increment the counter.

tasks.title: Shortest path in a maze
tasks.statement: Write a function maze_steps(grid): grid is a list of strings made of '.' (passage) and '#' (wall). Return the minimum number of steps from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner (a step goes to a neighboring cell horizontally or vertically), or -1. The field is up to 501×501: breadth-first search is needed.
tasks.hint: A queue of cells with distances and a visited list; neighbors only inside the field and not walls.

tasks.title: Disjoint set union
tasks.statement: Define a class UnionFind(n): elements 0..n-1, each initially in its own set. Methods: find(x) is the representative of the set, union(a, b) merges, connected(a, b), and the attribute count is the number of sets. Path compression and union by size are required: the check performs a million operations.
tasks.hint: parent[i] = i; find with path compression (iteratively!); union by size; on a merge, count -= 1.
